newsitem.title: USA: Bankamerica cutting 3,700 jobs, taking $280 million charge.
newsitem.headline: Bankamerica cutting 3,700 jobs, taking $280 million charge.

text.p: BankAmerica Corp. said Thursday that it would cut about 3,700 jobs and take a pre-tax charge of $280 million in a major restructuring of its business activities.
The company said the charge will result in a $165 million reduction in net income in the fourth quarter.

"We are changing our business mix in both Europe and Japan based on changing markets and we are streamlining our operations activities around the world," Chairman David A. Coulter said in a statement.
"We expect that almost all of these restructurings will be accomplished in 1997, and that the charge will be recovered in cost savings by the end of 1998."
He said the company will be reducing staff and restructuring units in mature European markets while expanding activities in emerging European markets.
In Japan, the charge relates to a previously announced restructuring of the Tokyo branch's activities and anticipated staff reductions caused by reduced demand for traditional credit products there.

The company also said it will close about 120 branches in California during 1997 while adding to other retail services. The bank currently operates about 1,400 retail outlets, as well as 3,800 ATMs, in the state.

"Eliminating positions is always difficult," Coulter said. "However, we have learned that it is better to take such action when the company is performing well, as BankAmerica is today. For instance, the likelihood of placing employees in other positions is better in good circumstances."
